title: Schneider–Stuhler resolution theorem (depth-zero baseline)
body_html:
Schneider–Stuhler resolution / equivalence theorem

Theorem [Schneider–Stuhler, Thm V.1]. For a $p$-adic reductive group $G$ with the standard Moy–Prasad cosheaf $G_{\bullet, 0+}$ and trivial character, $H_0$ induces an equivalence $$\Coeff_G^0(\mathcal{B}(G))[E_0^{-1}] \;\simeq\; \Rep_0(G).$$

This is the depth-zero baseline that Main Theorem 8.2.1: Rep_Φ(G) ≃ Rep_0(M) generalizes: rather than working with the standard building $\mathcal{B}(G)$ and trivial character, the §8 theorem uses the generalized building $\BSigma$ with a non-trivial semisimple character $\Phi$ and shows the resulting category $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ matches $\Rep_0(M)$ for the depth-zero Levi $M$.

Connection to the Bestvina–Savin contraction

Schneider–Stuhler's original proof uses the polysimplicial structure on $\mathcal{B}(G)$ and a contraction at integer depth. Bestvina–Savin's generalization to DeBacker's $r$-facets (App C of the paper) extends this to arbitrary depth and is what lets the present work apply the same template to $\BSigma$.
